new_need.sentence: How many people actually read LindyBooks these days?

questions.question: How many distinct real people actually read LindyBooks in the recent period?
questions.quantity: Distinct human individuals who actually read content (engaged with the reading content, not merely landing on or loading a page) on LindyBooks within the window
questions.population: Distinct human readers of LindyBooks content who engaged with it, deduplicated across devices/sessions where possible
exclude: one-page bounces or visitors who never engaged with reading content
duplicate counts of the same person across sessions/devices
repeat counts of the same person across days within the window

capabilities.built_for: I want to know, at a glance, how many real people are actually using LindyBooks.
questions: How many distinct real human people have actually used LindyBooks recently?
How does the count of actively-using real people compare to total registered accounts?
metrics: How many distinct real human people have actually used LindyBooks rec…
Proxy: Daily usage count against the prose translation… (last 24h)

relation.description: same_need: built to answer what the new need asks (however well it answers today); can_do: the new request is something it can already do through its interface, as it is; extend: it holds the data or is the place the principal uses for this, but lacks something the request needs; unrelated

covered.description: ids of the new questions or requirements it covers

gaps.description: what the new need asks that it cannot do today

gaps: Its metrics are proxies (paid payments, 24h translation usage), not distinct readers who engaged with reading content
Unclear if it excludes bots, internal users and one-page bounces, or deduplicates people across devices
Unknown whether it supports 7d/30d/90d windows; the proxy is 24h only
Counts 'using' rather than 'reading', so subscribers who did not read may be included
